intro.title: useOnlineStatus
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useOnlineStatus` that tracks whether the user's browser is currently online or offline. You will learn how to use the browser's `navigator.onLine` property and the `online`/`offline` window events to monitor network connectivity in real-time. The main technologies involved are React hooks, specifically `useState` for state management and `useEffect` for handling side effects like event listeners. By the end, you'll have a reusable hook that returns a boolean value, allowing any component to easily respond to changes in network status.
intro.usecase: The useOnlineStatus hook is essential for building resilient applications that handle network connectivity changes gracefully. In real-world products like Google Docs or Figma, you'll see status indicators that show 'Offline' or 'Syncing' when internet connection drops, preventing data loss. E-commerce checkout flows use this pattern to disable payment buttons and show warnings when users lose connectivity mid-transaction. Streaming platforms like Netflix or YouTube implement similar logic to pause playback and display reconnection messages when network issues occur. Developers use this hook to create better user experiences by adapting UI behavior based on real-time network availability.
